1use alloc::vec;
2use alloc::vec::Vec;
3
4use crate::third_party::hayro_jbig2::arithmetic_decoder::{ArithmeticDecoder, ArithmeticDecoderContext};
5
6/// The integer arithmetic decoder (A.2).
7pub(crate) struct IntegerDecoder {
8    /// `CX` - Context memory for the integer decoder.
9    contexts: Vec<ArithmeticDecoderContext>,
10}
11
12impl IntegerDecoder {
13    /// Create a new integer decoder with fresh contexts.
14    #[inline(always)]
15    pub(crate) fn new() -> Self {
16        Self {
17            // A.2: "Each arithmetic integer decoding procedure requires 512 bytes of
18            // storage for its context memory."
19            contexts: vec![ArithmeticDecoderContext::default(); 512],
20        }
21    }
22
23    /// The integer arithmetic decoding procedure (A.2, Figure A.1).
24    ///
25    /// Returns `Some(value)` on success, or `None` if OOB (out-of-band) is decoded.
26    #[inline(always)]
27    pub(crate) fn decode(&mut self, decoder: &mut ArithmeticDecoder<'_>) -> Option<i32> {
28        // A.2 step 1: "Set: PREV = 1"
29        // `PREV` - Context prefix, contains bits decoded so far plus a leading 1.
30        let mut prev: u32 = 1;
31
32        // A.2 step 2: "Follow the flowchart in Figure A.1. Decode each bit with
33        // CX equal to 'IAx + PREV' where 'IAx' represents the identifier of the
34        // current arithmetic integer decoding procedure, '+' represents
35        // concatenation, and the rightmost 9 bits of PREV are used."
36
37        // `S` - Sign bit.
38        let s = self.decode_bit(decoder, &mut prev);
39
40        // `V` - Magnitude value, decoded according to Figure A.1 flowchart.
41        #[expect(clippy::same_functions_in_if_condition, reason = "each call mutates `prev`")]
42        let v = if self.decode_bit(decoder, &mut prev) == 0 {
43            // Figure A.1: "V = next 2 bits"
44            self.decode_n_bits(decoder, &mut prev, 2)
45        } else if self.decode_bit(decoder, &mut prev) == 0 {
46            // Figure A.1: "V = (next 4 bits) + 4"
47            self.decode_n_bits(decoder, &mut prev, 4) + 4
48        } else if self.decode_bit(decoder, &mut prev) == 0 {
49            // Figure A.1: "V = (next 6 bits) + 20"
50            self.decode_n_bits(decoder, &mut prev, 6) + 20
51        } else if self.decode_bit(decoder, &mut prev) == 0 {
52            // Figure A.1: "V = (next 8 bits) + 84"
53            self.decode_n_bits(decoder, &mut prev, 8) + 84
54        } else if self.decode_bit(decoder, &mut prev) == 0 {
55            // Figure A.1: "V = (next 12 bits) + 340"
56            self.decode_n_bits(decoder, &mut prev, 12) + 340
57        } else {
58            // Figure A.1: "V = (next 32 bits) + 4436"
59            self.decode_n_bits(decoder, &mut prev, 32).wrapping_add(4436)
60        };
61
62        // A.2: "The result of the integer arithmetic decoding procedure is equal to:
63        // - V if S = 0
64        // - -V if S = 1 and V > 0
65        // - OOB if S = 1 and V = 0"
66        if s == 0 {
67            Some(v as i32)
68        } else if v > 0 {
69            // Wrapping: `V` can be 2^31, whose negative is `i32::MIN`, as the cast already reads it.
70            Some((v as i32).wrapping_neg())
71        } else {
72            None
73        }
74    }
75
76    /// Decode a single bit and update `PREV` (A.2 step 3).
77    ///
78    /// A.2 step 3: "After each bit is decoded: If PREV < 256 set:
79    /// PREV = (PREV << 1) OR D. Otherwise set:
80    /// PREV = (((PREV << 1) OR D) AND 511) OR 256"
81    #[inline(always)]
82    fn decode_bit(&mut self, decoder: &mut ArithmeticDecoder<'_>, prev: &mut u32) -> u32 {
83        let ctx_idx = (*prev & 0x1FF) as usize;
84        // `D` - The just-decoded bit.
85        let d = decoder.read_bit(&mut self.contexts[ctx_idx]);
86
87        // A.2 step 3: Update PREV.
88        if *prev < 256 {
89            *prev = (*prev << 1) | d;
90        } else {
91            // A.2: "PREV always contains the values of the eight most-recently-
92            // decoded bits, plus a leading 1 bit, which is used to indicate the
93            // number of bits decoded so far."
94            *prev = (((*prev << 1) | d) & 511) | 256;
95        }
96
97        d
98    }
99
100    /// Decode `n` bits and update `PREV` for each.
101    #[inline(always)]
102    fn decode_n_bits(&mut self, decoder: &mut ArithmeticDecoder<'_>, prev: &mut u32, n: usize) -> u32 {
103        let mut value = 0_u32;
104        for _ in 0..n {
105            let bit = self.decode_bit(decoder, prev);
106            value = (value << 1) | bit;
107        }
108        value
109    }
110}
